Since the text and audio content provided by BLB represent a range of evangelical traditions, all of the ideas and principles conveyed in the resource materials are not necessarily affirmed, in total, by this ministry.

Blue Letter Bible study tools make reading, searching and studying the Bible easy and rewarding.

passages.title: 2 Chron. 24:1–27
passages.text: Loosely adapted from 2 Kings 11:21–12:21 , supplemented with the Chronicler’s own material (see 2 Chron. 24:27 ).

passages.title: 2 Chron. 24:5–6,  9
passages.text: **repair the house of your God**. See note on 2 Kings 12:4–5 .

passages.title: 2 Chron. 24:8–11
passages.text: **all the people rejoiced and brought their tax**. See 1 Chron. 29:6–9 . The Chronicler wants his readers to see God’s service at the temple not as a burden but as a joyful duty (see Ex. 36:2–7 ).

passages.title: 2 Chron. 24:15–22
passages.text: Jehoiada’s burial **among the kings** is unique for a high priest. **the king listened to them**. Without Jehoiada’s influence, Joash follows evil advice.

passages.title: 2 Chron. 24:23–27
passages.text: Judah’s defeat by the smaller Syrian army is a sign of divine judgment.

notes.text: **Joash did what was right**. See note on 2 Kings 12:2–3 .
**got for him two wives**. Jehoiada acts to ensure that the Davidic line will continue after being nearly destroyed by Athaliah.
**restore**. Athaliah and her family had defiled and damaged the temple (v. 7 ).
The revival of temple worship lasted **all the days of Jehoiada**. After Jehoiada dies and is no longer there to guide him, Joash becomes spiritually unfaithful.
